label: Capacity Counter + Remote-RED + Multi-Location MQTT
info: Multi-location capacity counter flow. Node-RED is authoritative: devices and Remote-RED publish commands to counters/<location>/capacity/command; Node-RED stores per-location state and publishes retained counters/<location>/capacity/state. Battery topics use counters/<location>/<device>/battery. Legacy single-location behavior defaults to mccarthys where needed.

name: Multi-location defaults
info: Default location fallback is mccarthys. Location-specific MQTT topics use counters/<location>/capacity/command, counters/<location>/capacity/state, and counters/<location>/<device>/battery.

name: Apply increment/decrement/reset
Publish current state
Remote-RED action → counter command
External state guard
info: Node-RED is authoritative. This flow watches counters/<location>/capacity/state. If a device publishes a non-authoritative state that disagrees with Node-RED's stored value, Node-RED republishes its authoritative retained value.

name: Guard authoritative state
Per-device MQTT battery logic
info: Battery input topic: counters/<location>/<device>/battery. Legacy counters/<device>/battery is still accepted and mapped to location mccarthys. Normalized output is counters/<location>/<device>/battery/normalized. Summary output is counters/<location>/capacity/battery/summary.

name: Normalize/store device battery
MQTT time authority for StopWatch RTC sync
info: Node-RED publishes retained time so StopWatch devices can set system time after boot and periodically correct drift. Firmware should subscribe to system/time/epoch and call settimeofday() from the received Unix epoch seconds.

name: Build retained MQTT time messages
